name: crew-panel-short-viewport
description: Regression for the tutorial step 8 report: on a short browser window the Crew panel's Training section (and everything else below the fold) had no way to scroll into view. One root cause, in CrewPanel.ts: the expandable roster row carries overflow:hidden for its rounded corners, which drops that row's automatic flex min-height from content-based to 0. Without a min-height floor the panel body's flex layout compressed an expanded row down to the space available instead of leaving it at natural size and overflowing the body the way a scrollable list does — so bodyEl.scrollHeight sat exactly equal to clientHeight (472=472, nothing to scroll at all) and the body's own overflow-y:auto was a no-op. flex-shrink:0 on the row is the fix. UIManager.ts's leftCol keeps max-height (not height): when the column's content overflows, max-height clamps its used height to a definite value, which is exactly what each panel's own max-height:100% resolves against — reverting that line alone keeps this scenario green, while reverting the roster row's flex-shrink:0 fails it, which is how the single root cause was isolated. Proving it needs a real wheel gesture: clickSelector and expect.usable/blocked both call Element.scrollIntoView internally before acting (interaction-executor.ts's clickSelector; interaction-driver.ts's blockedReason, deliberately, for the ordinary case of a row below the fold in a genuinely scrollable list), a DOM API no player has an equivalent for and one that is not gated by pointer-events — it would have scrolled straight past the bug undetected. This file dispatches mousemove + wheel through Puppeteer's CDP input pipeline, the way a genuine gesture hit-tests, then reads bodyEl's own scrollTop. The read is `waitForProperty` rather than a bare `assert` because page.mouse.wheel() resolving does not mean Chrome has committed the scroll — it can land on the compositor thread after the CDP call returns, which is what turned CI red on this very scenario (PR #888, shard 6/10, Chrome 127: 'expected scrollTop=50, got 0', reproducible there and never locally on Chrome 141 with a dedicated browser per run). waitForProperty polls for the value instead of padding with a fixed delay, so it costs only the time the browser actually takes and still fails by name, reporting the last scrollTop it saw, when the scroll never lands — which is what the negative control depends on.

steps.description: Employees #1 and #2 — two drillers, so the crew keeps changing activity (walking to the site, working it) while the roster is open (#1592). The first is the tutorial's own train-driller subject; courses grant new qualifications only (#1388), so the driller (who starts with blasting and driving.drill_rig) takes the rock fragmenter licence.
The only school that teaches driving.rock_fragmenter — no role starts with it (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATIONS).

#1592 regression, part 1. Command is a harmless placeholder (command mode has no 'wheel-scroll a panel'). While the driving_center is still a construction order, shrink to 1280x600, open Crew, expand employee #1 and wheel-scroll the roster by a real gesture. The Train button is not asserted here — it only exists once the school stands.

expect.note: No expect.usable here on purpose: it calls scrollIntoView, which would move the roster off the scrollTop 50 the wheel left and that part 2 asserts survives.

steps.description: Drive the driving_center site to completion while the Crew panel stays open and scrolled — both drillers walk to the site and work it, so their activity changes every few ticks. Before #1592 each change rebuilt the roster and snapped its scroll back to 0.

#1592 regression, part 2. The ticks of the previous step changed the crew's activity repeatedly; the roster must still sit where the wheel left it (scrollTop 50 — a refresh may not teleport it back). Nothing in this step re-expands the card or scrolls: employee #1's row is still open from part 1. The Train button is reachable by the same wheel gesture.

expect.note: The scroll position survived the whole construction (asserted twice, before and after the Train button appeared); the button is reachable.

steps.description: Completes the train-driller target. NOTE (#1592): the harness has no 'click by selector without scrollIntoView' action — clickSelector's own scrollIntoView still runs here. The regression is therefore proven by the scrollTop asserts above, not by this click; when such an action exists, switch this step to it.
